title: GeneralSparse: Bridging the Gap in SpMM for Pruned Large Language Model Inference on GPUs
problem: Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) kernels for GPU inference struggle to efficiently handle the irregular sparsity patterns produced by pruning in Large Language Models. Existing sparse libraries either target fixed sparsity structures or revert to dense computation, failing to bridge pruning efficiency with practical GPU performance.
motivation: Pruned LLMs can significantly reduce model size and inference latency, but current GPU SpMM implementations do not adapt to variable pruning patterns, limiting real-world speedups from sparsity.
method: GeneralSparse builds an efficient sparse matrix multiplication (SpMM) system that handles pruned neural networks, where weights are zeroed to compress the model. Rather than assuming all networks have the same sparsity pattern, it analyzes the specific pattern during inference and automatically selects the fastest computation method, arranges data efficiently in GPU memory, and compiles the calculation on-the-fly to maintain speed across varying sparsity densities and granularities.
key_novelty: A sparse multiplication engine that adapts to any irregular pattern from pruning without requiring fixed structure types or reverting to dense computation.
contributions: A general-purpose SpMM implementation supporting variable sparsity patterns from LLM pruning
GPU kernel optimizations achieving practical speedups for pruned transformer inference
Evaluation demonstrating improvements over cuSPARSE and other sparse GEMM libraries
Analysis of sparsity pattern characteristics and GPU efficiency tradeoffs
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in title; unclear whether work addresses dynamic sparsity patterns, distributed inference, or hardware constraints.
primary_theme: Adaptive sparse matrix multiplication for efficient pruned LLM inference
